value: Tijani, M.E.H., Zondag, H. and Van Delft, Y. (2022). Review of Electric Cracking of Hydrocarbons. ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering 10(49), 16070-16089. https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.2c03427

A TNO review (Perspective) of electric cracking. Loaded: conventional naphtha cracker SEC (26-31 GJ/t ethylene, reprinted from Ren 2006), furnace efficiency, CO2 (1.8-2 t/t ethylene, Ren 2006), typical furnace size (100 MW); licensor SEC per t ethylene (Table 1, reprinted from Worrell 2008); electric options for steam cracking: resistance e-furnace (laboratory; equivalent furnace 50 MW), induction (laboratory), Coolbrook RDR (bench 20 kg/h, pilot 400 kg/h planned; 20-40 MW motors, 7-16 reactors per Mt/yr ethylene, yield 38.3% vs 30.8%, reprinted from Johannesdahl and Purola 2021); Huels and DuPont arc/plasma acetylene reactors (kWh/kg acetylene, efficiency, dates); generic electric heater efficiencies and maximum temperatures; SMR SEC and CO2 (reprinted). The review gives no SEC for any electric cracker and no costs (only qualitative: CAPEX lower, OPEX higher; naphtha about 80% of ethylene cost). No TRLs stated; state-of-development rows paraphrase the text. Not loaded: laboratory-scale study details (shock tubes, sonolysis, DBD plasma), patent counts, other cracking processes (FCC, hydrocracking, visbreaking, coking) beyond their operating conditions. Locators are printed journal page numbers (16070-16089; PDF page = printed - 16069). Most numbers are reprinted and flagged; per-ethylene values are per t ethylene, not per t HVC.
